[Who calls plays for every NFL team in 2025? What to know] The 2025 NFL season is underway, which means we got our first look at new playcallers such as the Detroit Lions ' John Morton, Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' Josh Grizzard and the Super Bowl champion Philadelphia Eagles ' Kevin Patullo in Week 1. We also saw some recognizable faces in new places, as Ben Johnson took over as Chicago Bears head coach, Kellen Moore as New Orleans Saints HC and Brian Schottenheimer with the Dallas Cowboys . Each of them will carry the dual responsibility of coaching and calling offensive plays. Meanwhile, veteran coaches Andy Reid ( Kansas City Chiefs ), Sean Payton ( Denver Broncos ) and Sean McVay ( Los Angeles Rams ) continue to churn out creative offensive systems. And Josh McDaniels is back for his third stint as the New England Patriots ' offensive coordinator, aiming to push second-year quarterback Drake Maye to another level. Will Klint Kubiak continue to get the most out of Jayden Daniels with the Washington Commanders ? Will Arthur Smith and Aaron Rodgers stay in sync with the Pittsburgh Steelers ? How about new Jacksonville Jaguars coach Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence ? Here is who is calling plays for all 32 teams (with a key stat provided by ESPN Research). messages.content: [NBA buzz: Latest on trades, news, roster moves and intel] The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks . The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics , and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season. Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo 's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season? All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders. Quick links: Free agency grades | Trade grades Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz Depth charts | Trade machine | More Nov. 4 NBA Trade Lab updates: Porzingis is popular in mock deals In the first weeks since the release of ESPN Analytics' new NBA Trade Lab , the player involved in the most fan-created trades is Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis , who's in the news because the franchise is withholding payments from him while he's away from the team . With 38-year-old legend Stephen Curry still playing at an elite level, it makes sense that fans want to see the Warriors make a swing to bolster his supporting cast. Add to that how good rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has looked to start the season, and Warriors fans might be right to think their favorite team isn't that far away from contention in the West, especially considering the early-season injury problems for the Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves . Porzingis' $20 million salary would be a key ingredient for the Warriors to match salary in a potential trade. Below are some of the top fan-created trades involving Porzingis, as scored by fans voting from the perspective of each team involved: Trade No. 1 Warriors get: A shot-blocking stretch big in Myles Turner who could be a great fit in their motion-heavy offense to replicate some of Porzingis' game. Milwaukee Bucks get: Porzingis and a young promising player in Moses Moody , who could be more valuable for the Bucks' rebuild. Moody is recovering from a torn left patellar tendon he suffered in March. Trade No. 2 Warriors get: Daniel Gafford , who can provide rim protection and elite play-finishing. He would bolster their center depth and better exploit defenses that are stretched thin out on the perimeter drawn to Curry's gravity. Dallas Mavericks get: Porzingis and a first-round pick swap to help reset their timeline around 19-year-old centerpiece Cooper Flagg , by improving their assets in a potentially loaded 2028 draft. Trade No. 3 Warriors get: Talented 6-foot-8 forward Trey Murphy III , who can defend, draw fouls and rain 3s from well beyond the arc.
